Practical 1: Horizontal and Vertical Scaling using Python Multithreading 
 
 
Aim: 
To implement and compare Horizontal Scaling and Vertical Scaling using Python multithreading 
by measuring their execution time, and to understand how scaling techniques improve resource 
utilization and performance in Cloud Computing. 
 
 
Theory: 
 
Introduction 
Cloud Computing enables applications to handle varying workloads by providing scalable 
computing resources. As the number of users or requests increases, cloud platforms must ensure 
that applications continue to perform efficiently without service interruption. This is achieved 
through scaling, which allows computing resources to be increased or decreased according to 
demand. 
Major cloud service providers such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, and 
Google Cloud Platform (GCP) provide scaling features that automatically allocate resources 
based on workload, ensuring high availability and better performance. 
Scaling techniques are mainly classified into:

1. Horizontal Scaling (Scaling Out/In) 
2. Vertical Scaling (Scaling Up/Down) 
 
 
 
Horizontal Scaling (Scaling Out) 
Horizontal Scaling refers to increasing the number of servers or virtual machines to distribute the 
workload among multiple systems. Instead of upgrading a single server, additional servers are 
added to share the processing tasks. 
For example, when an online shopping website receives heavy traffic during a sale, multiple 
server instances are created to process user requests simultaneously. 
Characteristics 
 
• Adds multiple servers or virtual machines. 
• Distributes workload across several systems. 
• Improves availability and fault tolerance. 
• Easily expands resources according to demand. 
 
Advantages 
• High reliability and availability. 
• Efficient load distribution. 
• Suitable for large-scale cloud applications. 
• Supports a large number of concurrent users. 
• Easy to increase or decrease resources. 
Disadvantages 
• More complex infrastructure.

• Requires load balancing mechanisms. 
• Data synchronization may be required. 
Applications 
• Google Search 
• Amazon 
• Netflix 
• Facebook 
• YouTube 
 
Vertical Scaling (Scaling Up) 
Vertical Scaling refers to increasing the hardware capacity of a single server by upgrading CPU, 
RAM, storage, or processing power instead of adding more servers. 
For example, upgrading a virtual machine from 2 CPU cores and 4 GB RAM to 8 CPU cores and 
32 GB RAM. 
Characteristics 
• Enhances the performance of one machine. 
• Simple to implement. 
• No load balancing required. 
• Limited by maximum hardware capacity. 
Advantages 
• Easy implementation. 
• No major changes in application architecture. 
• Suitable for applications that cannot be distributed. 
Disadvantages 
• Hardware upgrade limitations. 
• Single point of failure.

• Higher cost for large upgrades.

Python Multithreading 
Multithreading allows multiple tasks to execute concurrently within a single program. In Python, 
the threading module is used to create and manage threads, enabling parallel execution of 
independent tasks. 
Important Methods Used 
• Thread() – Creates a new thread. 
• start() – Starts thread execution. 
• join() – Waits until the thread completes execution. 
In this practical: 
• Horizontal Scaling is simulated by creating multiple threads that execute workloads 
simultaneously, representing multiple cloud servers. 
• Vertical Scaling is simulated by using a single thread with a larger workload, 
representing a more powerful server. 
Program Explanation

• Multiple threads are created. 
• Each thread performs the same workload independently. 
• Threads execute simultaneously. 
• Total execution time is measured.

Applications in Cloud Computing 
Scaling is an essential feature of cloud computing because it enables systems to efficiently 
manage changing workloads. It helps organizations to: 
• Handle increasing user requests. 
• Improve application performance. 
• Optimize resource utilization. 
• Reduce operational costs. 
• Maintain continuous service availability. 
• Prevent system overload during peak traffic. 
Common applications include: 
• E-commerce websites during seasonal sales. 
• Banking and financial systems. 
• Online gaming platforms. 
• Video streaming services. 
• Cloud-hosted enterprise applications.
